quizzes.title: Origin of the day: MCQ practice
quizzes.passage: National Technology Day is observed in India on 11 May each year. It is a day set aside to commemorate major technological achievements, and it recalls a series of milestones the country reached on one particular date. Those milestones spanned different areas of work. One was related to nuclear research, one to aviation, and one to defence development carried out by a national research organisation. The day was given formal recognition by a senior national leader, and it has been observed every year since the first full year of observance. The name of the day has remained the same since it was first observed. Because it falls on a fixed date, the day gives the public a regular occasion to look back at how science and engineering have contributed to the country. The observance does not celebrate a single invention. Instead, it groups several achievements together under one date and one name. The milestones belonged to the same period of work, which is why they are remembered together. Each year the day keeps these achievements in the national calendar, linking past progress with present interest in technology. Its origins therefore lie in a specific set of events rather than in a general idea of progress alone.

questions.q: What was the theme of National Technology Day 2026?
questions.explanation: The booklet states that the 2026 observance carried the theme 'Responsible Innovation for Inclusive Growth'.

questions.q: Which agency test-fired the Trishul short-range surface-to-air missile on the day the observance commemorates?
questions.explanation: The booklet says DRDO successfully test-fired the Trishul missile on that day.

questions.q: In which year were the technological achievements commemorated by the day recorded?
questions.explanation: The commemorated achievements date to 11 May 1998, the year of the Pokhran-II tests and the Hansa-3 flight.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The Rashtriya Vigyan Puraskar awards are announced on National Technology Day.
Reason (R): The Rashtriya Vigyan Puraskar is India's science honour, comparable to the Padma Awards.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements are true, but the reason about the award's status does not explain why it is announced on this day.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Atal Bihari Vajpayee   ->   A. Declared the day as National Technology Day
II. Pokhran-II   ->   B. Series of nuclear tests in Rajasthan's Thar Desert
III. Hansa-3   ->   C. Aircraft that completed its first successful test flight
IV. Trishul   ->   D. Short-range surface-to-air missile
Choose the correct option.
questions.explanation: The booklet links Vajpayee with the declaration, Pokhran-II with the Thar Desert tests, Hansa-3 with a test flight and Trishul with a short-range missile.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. Hansa-3 completed its first successful test flight on the day commemorated.
II. The day was declared in 2000 by a prime minister.
III. The day has been observed annually from 1999 onward.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and III match the booklet, while II is wrong because the declaration was made in 1998.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements are correct?
I. The Pokhran-II tests were conducted in the Thar Desert of Rajasthan.
II. Trishul is a long-range ballistic missile.
III. The Hansa-3 test flight took place on the day commemorated.
questions.explanation: Statements I and III are correct, while II is wrong because Trishul is a short-range surface-to-air missile.

quizzes.title: Origin of the day: typed answers
quizzes.passage: National Technology Day is an observance in India that recognises technological achievement. It is based on a set of milestones that the country reached on one day, and the observance was created to remember them. The occasion is observed every year, and it has been part of the national calendar since its early years. The achievements it recalls belong to different fields of work. Some were linked to nuclear research, some to flight and some to the development of missiles. The observance does not celebrate one invention alone. Its name has stayed the same since the first observance, and the day is treated as a fixed point on the calendar. A national leader of the time gave the day its formal status, which is why the observance is linked to a specific decision rather than a general idea. Another part of the day's background involves the national awards for science, which are announced on the occasion. The day therefore brings together several strands: a historical date, a list of technical milestones, a formal decision by a leader, and a regular annual observance that keeps these achievements in view for the public. Each observance returns attention to the same set of achievements.

questions.q: Which Prime Minister declared 11 May as National Technology Day? (full name)
questions.explanation: The booklet says PM Atal Bihari Vajpayee declared 11 May as National Technology Day in 1998.

questions.q: In which year did the annual observance of the day begin? (year)
questions.explanation: The booklet states the day has been observed annually as National Technology Day from 1999 onward.

questions.q: Which agency test-fired the Trishul missile on that day? (acronym)
questions.explanation: The booklet says DRDO successfully test-fired the Trishul short-range surface-to-air missile.

questions.q: Which aircraft completed its first successful test flight on that day? (name with hyphen)
questions.explanation: The booklet states that the Hansa-3 aircraft completed its first successful test flight on that day.

questions.q: In which desert is the Pokhran test range located? (name of the desert)
questions.explanation: The booklet places the Pokhran test range in Rajasthan's Thar Desert.

questions.q: What are India's science honours that are announced on the day called? (name of the awards)
questions.explanation: The booklet names the Rashtriya Vigyan Puraskar awards as India's science honours, announced annually on National Technology Day.

questions.q: Which series of nuclear tests was conducted in May 1998? (name)
questions.explanation: The booklet describes the nuclear test series of May 1998 as Pokhran-II.

quizzes.title: Digital, farm and dairy milestones: MCQ practice
quizzes.passage: National Technology Day also draws attention to India's progress in digital infrastructure, farm output and dairy. These achievements are not limited to laboratories. They affect how citizens pay for goods, how farmers grow food and how milk reaches households. The observance groups these areas together with the country's scientific and engineering work. International assessments also compare countries on innovation, patents and intellectual property, and these comparisons are published by global bodies. Such assessments are referred to in discussions about the country's technological standing. The observance therefore links everyday technology with national standing. Each year, the day offers a chance to look at these developments together, including the systems that run across the country and the changes in food and dairy production. These achievements show how technology has entered ordinary life. They form a second strand of the observance, alongside the milestones that the day recalls from its origin. The areas are varied, which is why the day is treated as a broad recognition of technological progress rather than of one sector alone. Their scope is one reason the observance is wider than a single anniversary of one event.

questions.q: Which organisation's report is cited for India's intellectual property filings?
questions.explanation: The booklet cites the WIPO report for India's sixth-place position in intellectual property filings.

questions.q: Which index is cited for India's 2026 innovation standing?
questions.explanation: The booklet cites the Global Innovation Index 2026 for India's innovation standing.

questions.q: Which system is described as the world's largest biometric ID system?
questions.explanation: The booklet describes Aadhaar as the world's largest biometric ID system.

questions.q:

Choose the correct option.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: The booklet says the Green Revolution boosted production through high-yielding wheat and rice varieties, so R explains A.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:

II. UPI   ->   B. Revolutionised digital payments
III. Green Revolution   ->   C. High-yielding wheat and rice varieties

questions.explanation: Each item matches its booklet description in option C: Aadhaar, UPI, the Green Revolution and the White Revolution.

Consider the following statements:

II. UPI was launched as a biometric identity system.
III. The WIPO report is cited for India's intellectual property filings.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and III match the booklet, whereas II wrongly describes UPI as a biometric identity system.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements are correct?
I. Aadhaar is the world's smallest biometric ID system.
II. The Green Revolution used high-yielding wheat and rice varieties.
III. The 2026 observance theme was 'Responsible Innovation for Inclusive Growth'.
questions.explanation: Only statements II and III are correct, since Aadhaar is described as the world's largest, not smallest, biometric ID system.

quizzes.title: Digital, farm and dairy milestones: typed answers
quizzes.passage: National Technology Day also highlights India's digital infrastructure and farm and dairy milestones. Digital systems now reach large numbers of people in their everyday lives, and the observance treats them as a major area of progress. Farm output and dairy production have also changed over several decades, and these changes are placed alongside the country's scientific work. Several indices and reports from global bodies are used to discuss how the country performs in innovation and intellectual property. Such reports are referred to in discussions about technological standing, and they are part of the wider picture the observance describes. The day therefore brings together technology in daily life with national performance in research. Its framework covers machines, laboratories and the systems that serve citizens directly. The observance does not focus on a single sector. Instead, it treats digital, agricultural and dairy progress as connected parts of one story about technological development in India. Each year, the day gives the public an occasion to review these areas together and to consider the progress they represent. The areas are varied, but they share the theme of applying technology to national life.

questions.q: Which identity system is described as the world's largest biometric ID system? (name)

questions.q: Which revolution made India the world's largest milk producer? (name)
questions.explanation: The booklet states that the White Revolution made India the world's largest milk producer.

questions.q: Which index was cited for India's 2026 innovation standing? (short form)
questions.explanation: The booklet cites the Global Innovation Index for India's 2026 innovation standing.

questions.q: Which organisation's report is cited for India's intellectual property filings? (acronym)
questions.explanation: The booklet cites the WIPO report for India's intellectual property filings.

questions.explanation: UPI stands for Unified Payments Interface, as the booklet spells out.

quizzes.title: Institutions and schemes: MCQ practice
quizzes.passage: India runs a number of public bodies, missions and schemes that are meant to support technology. These institutions differ in their purpose. Some work on research and development, some support new companies, and some focus on the link between government needs and private innovation. A few programmes are designed for students, so that young people can take part in experiments and build practical skills early in their education. Others target specialised sectors where the country wants to develop its own capabilities. Some bodies were created by a specific Act, while others operate as programmes under national agencies. Some are led by national bodies, while others operate through government departments. Support can take the form of funding, training, facilities or access to expert networks. Together these arrangements form a support system that links science, industry and education. Each institution has its own role within this system. Some schemes are linked to national missions with defined focus areas. The variety of these arrangements is one reason the day is observed as a broad recognition of technological work. This variety is visible in the range of programmes that the country runs at once, in several sectors.

questions.q: Which mission, launched by NITI Aayog, aims to foster an innovation culture?
questions.explanation: The booklet states that the Atal Innovation Mission was launched by NITI Aayog to foster an innovation culture.

questions.q: What are Atal Tinkering Labs?
questions.explanation: The booklet describes Atal Tinkering Labs as innovation labs in schools.

questions.q: In which year was the Act that makes the Technology Development Board a statutory body passed?
questions.explanation: The booklet identifies the Technology Development Board as a statutory body under the Technology Development Board Act, 1995.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The Technology Development Board provides financial assistance to commercialise indigenous technologies.
Reason (R): The Technology Development Board supports the adaptation of imported technology for wider application.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements are true, but the second does not explain why the board gives financial assistance.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. iDEX   ->   A. Indigenous defence startups and MSMEs
II. NM-ICPS   ->   B. R&D in AI, Robotics, IoT and Quantum Computing
III. IN-SPACe and NSIL   ->   C. Private sector participation in the space programme
IV. Atal Incubation Centres   ->   D. Support for startups
Choose the correct option.
questions.explanation: The booklet pairs iDEX with defence startups, NM-ICPS with R&D in AI and related fields, IN-SPACe with private participation in space, and Atal Incubation Centres with startup support.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. The Technology Development Board promotes the commercialisation of indigenous technology.
II. Make in India was launched in 2014 to boost domestic manufacturing.
III. The National Quantum Mission focuses only on quantum computing.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and II match the booklet, while III is wrong because the mission also covers communication, sensing and materials.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements are correct?
I. The National Supercomputing Mission plans to install a network of world-class supercomputers across premier institutions.
II. INSPIRE is a programme linked to DST that encourages science education and research careers.
III. iDEX supports defence startups only in the nuclear sector.
questions.explanation: Statements I and II are correct, while III is wrong because iDEX promotes indigenous defence startups and MSMEs generally.

quizzes.title: Institutions and schemes: typed answers
quizzes.passage: India supports technology through a mix of statutory bodies, national missions and smaller programmes. Some of these arrangements are created by a specific law, while others come from national planning bodies that set priorities for innovation. Schemes aim to help research reach the market, to encourage new ideas among young people and to build capacity in areas such as defence technology and emerging sciences. Support can come in the form of money, training, facilities or access to expert networks. Some bodies are directed at industry, others at schools and universities, and some work across several areas at once. The national awards for science also form part of this landscape. Each of these bodies has its own focus and its own method of working. The overall picture is one of institutions that complement one another, each with a defined area of work, and that together aim to strengthen national technological capability. Students, researchers and entrepreneurs are among the groups that these programmes are designed to reach. The range of these programmes shows how technology policy in India covers education, research, industry and defence at the same time. Students and schools form one part of this effort, while defence and space form another.

questions.q: Which body, set up under an Act of 1995, promotes the commercialisation of indigenous technology? (acronym)
questions.explanation: The booklet describes the Technology Development Board as a statutory body that promotes commercialisation of indigenous technology.

questions.q: Which defence startup scheme's name stands for Innovations for Defence Excellence? (short form)
questions.explanation: The booklet expands iDEX as Innovations for Defence Excellence, which promotes indigenous defence startups and MSMEs.

questions.q: In which year was the Technology Development Board Act passed? (year)
questions.explanation: The booklet cites the Technology Development Board Act, 1995.

questions.q: Which NITI Aayog-launched mission fosters an innovation culture? (short form)
questions.explanation: The booklet states that the Atal Innovation Mission, abbreviated AIM, was launched by NITI Aayog.

questions.q: Which national awards are comparable to the Padma Awards? (name)
questions.explanation: The booklet describes the Rashtriya Vigyan Puraskar awards as India's science honours, comparable to the Padma Awards.

questions.q: Which national mission focuses on quantum computing, communication, sensing and materials? (name)
questions.explanation: The booklet lists the National Quantum Mission as focusing on quantum computing, communication, sensing and materials.

questions.q: Which mission plans a network of world-class supercomputers across premier institutions? (name)
questions.explanation: The booklet states that the National Supercomputing Mission plans to install a network of world-class supercomputers.
